text:
Open Wearables

 Open-source, self-hosted wearable data layer: one API and one schema for the devices your users already wear. 

 
 
 
 
 

Website · Documentation · Quickstart · Providers · Roadmap

---

Open Wearables is an open-source platform that connects wearable devices and health apps, standardizes their data into one schema, and serves it through a single REST API. It runs inside your own cloud account, so data goes from each provider straight to your deployment without passing through a third party.

Instead of building and maintaining a separate integration for Garmin, Oura, Whoop, Polar, Apple Health, Samsung Health, Google Health Connect and the rest, you deploy one service. It handles provider OAuth, background sync, webhooks and mobile SDK uploads, and your product reads sleep, activity, workouts and heart rate the same way whatever device the data came from. A built-in MCP server lets LLMs and AI agents query the same data.

It is built for teams whose product runs on wearable data: digital health products and health data platforms, care programs, hospitals and telemedicine, remote patient monitoring, clinical research and more. See who runs Open Wearables in production.

 

 Why self-hosted

Open Wearables runs on your own infrastructure. In practice that means:

- You decide where the data lives. Deploy to whatever cloud and region your requirements call for (HIPAA, GDPR, internal policy) and control who has access.
- Provider apps and tokens belong to you. You register the developer apps with Garmin, Oura, Whoop and others under your own account, and OAuth tokens are stored in your database.
- Nobody sits between you and the provider. Data goes from the provider's API straight to your deployment, without passing through any third-party service.
- MIT licensed. Read the code, change it, fork it, run it in production. If you fix or build something others could use, we'd be happy to take it upstream. See the contributing guidelines to get started.

 How it works

1. Connect. A user links a wearable account through a connection link, or syncs Apple Health, Samsung Health or Health Connect from the phone through a mobile SDK.
2. Sync. Open Wearables pulls data through provider webhooks and scheduled syncs, including a historical backfill on first connection.
3. Standardize. Every record is mapped into one unified data model in your PostgreSQL database. If you want the originals too, raw provider payloads can be captured to S3 before processing.
4. Notify. Your app receives an outgoing webhook when new data arrives.
5. Query. Your app reads the data through one REST API, in the same shape whichever provider it came from.

 Supported providers

 Cloud providers , connected server to server through OAuth:

Garmin · Oura · Whoop · Polar · Suunto · Strava · Withings · Ultrahuman · SensorBio · Google Health · Fitbit (deprecated)

 On-device sources , read on the phone through the mobile SDKs:

Apple Health (HealthKit) · Google Health Connect · Samsung Health

 Apple Health export: upload a full Apple Health XML export, large files included.

See data coverage for what each provider delivers. Missing a provider? Check the open provider requests or read how to add a new provider.

 Data you get

 Category Examples 
 --- --- 
 Daily summaries Activity (steps, calories, intensity minutes), sleep, body, recovery 
 Sleep and workouts Sleep sessions with stages, naps, workouts with samples, personal records 
 Time series Heart rate, HRV, SpO2, weight, steps, energy and many more data types 
 Nutrition Meals with energy and macronutrients, from the sources that provide them 
 Women's health Menstrual cycle records 
 Provider metrics Values computed by the device provider itself, stored as reported and labeled with their source 

 Quickstart

Run Open Wearables locally with Docker in a few minutes.

 

 make init creates both .env files from their examples and generates SECRET KEY . Without make , copy them yourself and set SECRET KEY to the output of openssl rand -hex 32 (at least 32 characters, or the backend does not start).

- Developer portal: Create API keys and add provider credentials here.
- API docs (Swagger): 
- Sample data (optional): make seed creates test users with activity data.

 [!WARNING]
 An admin account is created on first startup from the ADMIN EMAIL and ADMIN PASSWORD variables (defaults: admin@admin.com / your-secure-password ). The seed runs only while no developer account exists, so changing ADMIN PASSWORD later does not update it. Set your own ADMIN PASSWORD before the first start, or change the default password in the developer portal right after your first login. With ENVIRONMENT=production the default password is refused: a fresh deployment does not start until ADMIN PASSWORD is set, and an admin that still has the default cannot sign in until you set ADMIN PASSWORD (with ADMIN EMAIL matching that account's email) and restart the backend, which then changes that account's password to it.

 Running in production 

 docker compose up builds from local source and is meant for development. On any server reachable from the internet set ENVIRONMENT=production , which refuses the default admin password. In production, run the official images pinned to a release tag, not nightly or a build of main :

- themomentum/open-wearables-backend 
- themomentum/open-wearables-frontend 

Follow the Docker deployment guide and read the release notes before upgrading.

 Local development without Docker 

See the local development setup in the docs and CONTRIBUTING.md.

 Features

 Unified API and data model

- One REST API with OpenAPI documentation, consistent regardless of the source device.
- Daily summaries, time series and events (workouts, sleep sessions) in a unified data model.
- Data priorities: decide which provider and device type wins when sources overlap.
- Multi-account sync: one provider account can be linked to several user profiles.

 Connections and sync

- OAu

install.title: Quickstart
install.html:
Run Open Wearables locally with Docker in a few minutes.

git clone https://github.com/the-momentum/open-wearables.git
cd open-wearables

make init
docker compose up -d

make init creates both .env files from their examples and generates SECRET_KEY. Without make, copy them yourself and set SECRET_KEY to the output of openssl rand -hex 32 (at least 32 characters, or the backend does not start).

  • Developer portal: http://localhost:3000. Create API keys and add provider credentials here.
  • API docs (Swagger): http://localhost:8000/docs
  • Sample data (optional): make seed creates test users with activity data.

[!WARNING] An admin account is created on first startup from the ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD variables (defaults: admin@admin.com / your-secure-password). The seed runs only while no developer account exists, so changing ADMIN_PASSWORD later does not update it. Set your own ADMIN_PASSWORD before the first start, or change the default password in the developer portal right after your first login. With ENVIRONMENT=production the default password is refused: a fresh deployment does not start until ADMIN_PASSWORD is set, and an admin that still has the default cannot sign in until you set ADMIN_PASSWORD (with ADMIN_EMAIL matching that account's email) and restart the backend, which then changes that account's password to it.

Running in production

docker compose up builds from local source and is meant for development. On any server reachable from the internet set ENVIRONMENT=production, which refuses the default admin password. In production, run the official images pinned to a release tag, not nightly or a build of main:

  • themomentum/open-wearables-backend
  • themomentum/open-wearables-frontend

Follow the Docker deployment guide and read the release notes before upgrading.

Local development without Docker

See the local development setup in the docs and CONTRIBUTING.md.

features.title: Features
features.html:
Unified API and data model
  • One REST API with OpenAPI documentation, consistent regardless of the source device.
  • Daily summaries, time series and events (workouts, sleep sessions) in a unified data model.
  • Data priorities: decide which provider and device type wins when sources overlap.
  • Multi-account sync: one provider account can be linked to several user profiles.
Connections and sync
  • OAuth flow management through a connection link: the user picks their provider, authenticates, and data starts syncing.
  • Historical backfill on first connection, within each provider's limits.
  • Live sync progress as a server-sent event stream, plus sync run history in the API and the portal.
Webhooks

Register HTTPS endpoints and get notified when new data arrives. Filter by event type or user, verify signatures, send test events and inspect every delivery attempt. Outgoing webhooks are off by default, see how to enable them in the webhooks guide.

Mobile SDKs and app

Apple Health, Samsung Health and Health Connect keep data on the phone, with no cloud API. The SDKs read it on the device and upload it to your deployment.

SDK Platform
iOS SDK Swift, Apple HealthKit
Android SDK Kotlin, Samsung Health and Google Health Connect
Flutter SDK Dart wrapper around the native SDKs
React Native SDK TypeScript wrapper around the native SDKs

No app of your own yet? A simple demo app syncs on-device health data to your instance with an invitation code (setup guide). TestFlight (iOS) and APK (Android) builds are available on request in Discord.

For production use, Open Wearables Connect, a full-featured app, is coming soon to the App Store and Google Play. A white-label version, published in the stores under your own brand, will be available as well.

MCP server for AI agents

A built-in Model Context Protocol server gives Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients access to your users' wearable data. Ask "How did John sleep last week?" and the model fetches the right records itself. Keep in mind that the records it fetches are sent to the model provider behind your MCP client.

Tools: get_users, get_activity_summary, get_sleep_summary, get_workout_events, get_timeseries, get_menstrual_cycles. Setup: MCP server docs.

Developer portal

A web dashboard with light and dark themes, usable on a phone:

  • Dashboard with users and data points at a glance.
  • Users: connected sources and data explorers for activity, sleep, workouts, body, meals and women's health.
  • Coverage and syncs: which data types each provider delivers, and every sync run.
  • Webhooks: endpoints and delivery debugging.
  • Settings: API keys, provider credentials, data priorities, data lifecycle, team invitations and a seed data generator.
Data lifecycle and raw payloads
  • Configurable archival and retention of time series data.
  • Optional raw payload storage: capture provider payloads exactly as they were sent, to logs or an S3 bucket, and replay them against new parsing logic. Disabled by default.
